sections.html:
Yukon lies in eastern Canadian County, about 16 miles west of downtown Oklahoma City, and covers roughly 26.5 square miles of land. Route 66 and highways 4 and 92 cross town, with Interstate 40 along the south edge. Two ZIP codes, 73085 and 73099, cover the city.

Population was 23,630 in 2020, spread over 9,258 households. Owners occupy 71.1% of homes. Rentals make up the other 28.9%, so landlords sell here as well. Most residents commute to jobs elsewhere in the metro, and a building boom starting in the 1960s produced much of the housing.

Yukon Public Schools covers most of the city, but parts of Yukon are zoned to Banner Public School and Riverside Public School instead. Confirm the district for your address before listing, since the mailing address can point to a different one than the zoning does.

The Yukon district had 9,597 students on October 1 of the 2024-25 year. Yukon High School, at 1777 South Yukon Parkway, reported 2,984 students, and Yukon Middle School, at 801 Garth Brooks Boulevard, reported 1,410.

Roofs take the beating in Oklahoma storms, and inspectors on Yukon sales look there first. The Oklahoma Insurance Department lists hail as the leading homeowners claim, and in higher-risk areas a policy may add its own wind or hail deductible.

Many insurers also discount impact-resistant roofing, and the state's OKReady program promotes FORTIFIED roof standards for wind and hail.

  • Save roofing invoices, claim letters and any papers on impact-resistant shingles.
  • Check the policy's wind or hail deductible before you choose between repairing and selling as-is.
  • With a claim still open, ask the insurer what a sale does to it before you sign.

Development Services at City Hall handles building, electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits. To ask for an inspection, call 405-354-6676 on weekdays between 8:30 a.m. and 5 p.m.

State law adds a $4 fee to every permit, plus a $0.50 city collection fee, beyond the city's posted schedule. Projects such as pools and pipelines need a full set of plans, including a plot plan, with the application.

Did you finish a garage or build a deck yourself? Learn whether it was permitted now, not when a buyer's inspector raises it.

Water comes through the city's Utility Billing department, which reads meters each month. Its web page has forms to start, stop or transfer service, and another to ask for a deposit back. Landlords use a separate authorization form to reactivate an account.

Time the stop or transfer to land on closing day and file the final meter read with your closing papers. Where a tenant held the account, make sure it is paid in full before the keys change hands.

sections.h2: What Oklahoma requires a Yukon seller to disclose
sections.html:
Under Oklahoma's Residential Property Condition Disclosure Act, a seller of a one or two unit home must hand over a disclosure statement or a disclaimer whenever a real estate licensee is involved or the buyer requests one in writing. The buyer needs it in hand before accepting an offer.

Topics on the form include water and sewer, flood zone status, roof, walls, foundation, wood-destroying insects and major fire or tornado damage. A statement dated more than 180 days before the buyer receives it is too old.

  • An owner who never lived there may sign a disclaimer saying they know of no defects.
  • A defect discovered after the form goes out means you must promptly send an amended one.
  • Some transfers are exempt, among them a non-occupying fiduciary acting for an estate, trust or guardianship, and sales after foreclosure.

Canadian County bills Yukon homes. Its assessor sets the value. The Canadian County Treasurer, located at 314 W. Rogers Street in El Reno, collects the money and passes it on to the county, cities, towns and schools.

City charges can stick to the house. Weed, cleaning, paving and nuisance abatement bills that the city levies are sent to the Treasurer when they go unpaid, and they become a lien on the tax account. Online payment fees run 1.95% on debit cards, 2.75% on credit cards and $1.50 for an eCheck. A returned check costs $35.

Search your parcel on the treasurer's tax roll site before listing and make sure no delinquent balance or city lien shows. The office answers at 405-295-6330 on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

sections.h2: Common reasons Yukon owners sell, and how a cash sale fits
sections.html:
Sellers here usually weigh time, repair cost and listing price against each other. Selling for cash to a buyer like us gives up some price in return for speed and no repair work.

  • Spring storm damage to the roof, siding or windows that is expensive to fix before listing.
  • An inherited house whose heirs live elsewhere and want the estate closed.
  • A rental with a tenant inside, or one that needs work between tenants.
  • A job move within the Oklahoma City metro on a tight schedule.
  • City charges or liens that must come out of the sale proceeds.

A cash offer has no lender appraisal and no loan approval to wait for, and the title company pays off liens at closing. We promise no price in advance. We see the house, then put a written offer in your hands so you can compare it with listing or selling on your own.

sections.h2: Steps from first call to closing
sections.html:
It goes quickly. First you describe the house. Next we view it. Then a written offer arrives. Once you accept, a title company opens the file, searches for liens and unpaid city charges, and books a closing date that fits your plans.

In the days before closing, book the water stop, gather roofing and permit papers, and check the parcel on the Canadian County tax roll. At signing, the title company clears any mortgage or lien from the proceeds and you take the remainder. No repairs are required beforehand.

Bring photo ID and the deed details if you have them, along with any unpaid utility or permit notices. Mention a tenant, an open insurance claim or a probate matter early, because each one changes who has to sign and how long the title work takes.

faqs.q: Is Yukon, OK in Oklahoma County or Canadian County?
faqs.a: Yukon is in eastern Canadian County. Property tax is billed by the Canadian County Treasurer in El Reno.

faqs.q: Which taxes do I owe when I sell a Yukon house?
faqs.a: Property tax for the year is the main one. How the current year is split between you and the buyer is set in the sale contract and handled by the title company, so check your closing statement.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a condition report in Yukon?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Oklahoma requires a seller of a one or two unit home to give a written disclosure or disclaimer before an offer is accepted when a real estate licensee is involved or the buyer asks in writing. Several transfers are exempt, such as those by a non-occupant fiduciary in an estate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Yukon house with storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. Hail and wind damage is common in Oklahoma, and a cash buyer can take the house as-is. If you have an open insurance claim, ask your insurer how a sale affects it before you sign.

faqs.q: How do I stop my Yukon water service at closing?
faqs.a: Use the stop or transfer service request on the City of Yukon Utility Billing page or call the department at 405-350-3910 on a weekday. Ask for a meter read on your closing date.
